沖繩美軍命案引爆民憤與官方應對

作者指出，沖繩那霸市日前發生一起震驚日本社會的命案，一名三十九歲日本女性在飯店遭勒斃且財物被洗劫，涉案嫌犯為一名二十歲的駐日美軍海軍陸戰隊士兵。事件曝光後，日本政府迅速做出強烈反應，外務大臣與防衛大臣分別召見美方官員抗議並要求嚴正徹查與整飭軍紀，首相亦痛批此為惡性犯罪。然而，美軍隨後採取的四十八小時軍事暫停、宵禁與教育宣導等措施，被沖繩民眾與地方首長批評為毫無實質效用的老調重彈，沖繩與東京等地相繼爆發抗議集會，輿論直指美軍基地集中在沖繩已非單純地方問題，而是全日本必須共同面對的政府治理缺失。

歷史傷痕與《美日地位協定》的權力傾斜

作者回顧自一九七二年沖繩主權回歸日本以來，美軍及其相關人員在當地犯罪頻傳。一九九五年的美軍性侵十二歲少女案引爆戰後沖繩最大規模的抗議浪潮，同時暴露出《美日地位協定》的不平等漏洞——美方在日方檢察官正式起訴前不需交出嫌犯，如同治外法權般重重阻礙日本警方的偵辦；雖然後續雙方針對重大重罪達成引渡磋商機制，但美軍仍保留裁量權。二〇一六年亦發生二十歲沖繩女性遭基地文職人員殺害的慘劇，再次凸顯美軍在沖繩的犯罪並非偶發個案，而是深層的體制性問題。

Okinawan girl, sparking the largest. anti-base protests in Okinawa since the. war. Organizers estimated 85,000 people. took to the streets, while Japanese. police estimated 60,000. the U.S. did not have to hand over. suspects to Japan until they were. formally indicted by Japanese. prosecutors. This meant Japanese police. could not detain the suspects during. the investigation and could only. conduct limited questioning with U.S. approval and presence; they had to wait. until prosecutors gathered enough. evidence to formally indict them before. the U.S. would hand them over. This. provision, which acts like. extraterritoriality, severely hindered. Japanese investigations and caused. intense dissatisfaction among Okinawans. . It eventually forced the U.S. and. Japan to negotiate a new mechanism,. allowing Japan to request the handover. of suspects before indictment in cases. of major crimes like murder or sexual. assault, though the U.S. still retains. discretion and it is not a mandatory. handover. Twenty years later, in 2016. A 20-year-old Okinawan woman, Rina. Shimabukuro, was murdered by a civilian. employee working at a U.S. military. base, leading to about 65,000 people. taking to the streets in protest. Barack Obama at the G7 Ise-Shima Summit. , later stating that their bilateral. meeting was almost entirely focused on. the Okinawa murder case. Japan's total land area, yet. approximately 70.3%of U.S. military. facilities in Japan are concentrated. there. On the main island of Okinawa. alone, U.S. bases occupy about 15%of. the land. Historians. studying U.S. military bases and. post-war Japan point out that the noise. , accidents, and social conflicts of. these bases are dumped onto a few. specific regions. Most people in Japan. are distanced from these costs; many do. not have to endure the sound of fighter. jets daily, nor do they face the risks. of having a base on their doorstep,. which leads to a stark difference in. perspective between the Japanese. mainland and Okinawa. Conversely, 31.8%of people. nationwide feel the status quo is fine. Indeed. However, as tensions between. China and the Taiwan Strait intensify,. Okinawa's voice becomes increasingly. critical. Less than a month ago,. Okinawa elected a new governor, Denny. Tamaki. Reuters analyzed that his. taking office might make it easier for. Tokyo to allow the Self-Defense Forces. and the U.S. military to use civilian. airports and ports in the Nansei. Islands. Because Yonaguni Island is. only about 110 kilometers from Taiwan,. Japan is deploying missile and. electronic warfare units across the.

southwest, making Okinawa's strategic. value on the first island chain higher. than ever. The problem is that Tamaki. has indicated he will not. unconditionally accept further. militarization, creating a dilemma for. Tokyo. He must show the people of. Okinawa and Japan that Japan won't stay. silent about major crimes against its. citizens just because it needs the US. military. Yet, on the other hand,. China-Japan relations are already poor,. and the US and China are trying to cool. tensions. Japan cannot afford a major. rift in its most important military. alliance. So far, the demands made to. the US have been limited to cooperating. with investigations, improving. discipline, and preventing recurrence. There have been no requests to revise. the US-Japan Status of Forces Agreement. , no demands to reduce troops in. Okinawa, and no halt to construction at. Futenma Base. When a similar incident. occurred in 2016, Shinzo Abe had the. opportunity to protest directly to. Obama during the G7 summit. As for. Takaichi, she rarely made the Okinawa. US base issue a central part of her. political platform. In other words,. while she is hawkish on diplomatic. rhetoric, her stance on the structural. core of the US-Japan alliance remains. very restrained. Behind this lies a. fundamental issue: Japan’s long-term. post-war national security relies on. the security umbrella provided by the. US. This structural dependency won't. easily change just by switching prime. ministers. Being too soft on the US is. unacceptable to Okinawa, but being. truly hard to the point of hostility is. something Japan cannot afford. This is. perhaps the most difficult part of. these cases to resolve. While watching. this news, I had a major question:.

living in the US, I don't feel the US. military's discipline is this poor. Do. they only become like this when they go. abroad? I used G-Men to look it up and. reached a few conclusions. First, as we. mentioned earlier, immense military. pressure is highly concentrated on a. small island, causing the risk of harm. to local residents to skyrocket. According to Japan's National Police. Agency, out of all US military-related. crimes in Japan, a staggering 72. percent are concentrated in Okinawa. Second, the extremely low conviction. rate. Restricted by the US-Japan Status. of Forces Agreement, Japanese police. struggle to investigate or arrest US. military personnel. Even when cases are. handed over to US military courts, the. conviction rate for sexual assault is. only about 10%, far lower than the. standards in the US. Most offending. soldiers avoid jail time, receiving. only minor punishments like written. reprimands, leaving the people of. Okinawa feeling deeply aggrieved. Putting myself in their shoes, if. Penghu became a US military base today. and these things happened to the people. there, wouldn't they be furious? I. think they would. 摘要

康乃爾大學性侵指控與調查爭議

影片作者以康乃爾大學一宗性侵指控為切入點。民事訴訟指稱，一名化名為「Jane Doe」的前學生於2024年10月前往校園內的 Psi Upsilon 兄弟會會所時，已飲酒至難以清醒同意；訴狀稱，她其後遭人要求飲用烈酒、吸食大麻，並遭多名男性學生侵犯，事件持續至清晨。這些內容屬於訴訟中的指控，案件仍待調查釐清。

Jane Doe 在事發近三週後向校園警方報案。訴狀稱，涉案七名學生一度遭校方暫停學籍，但校方也提供撰寫反省信以減輕處分的機會。據報導，她在警方訪談中表示自己確定遭到強暴，並稱當時已無法清醒作出同意；然而，警方將一份約120頁的訪談紀錄濃縮為六頁，短版紀錄未包含這項關鍵陳述。

報導指出，負責檢察官當時依據六頁紀錄，認為當事人的飲酒、用藥與性行為是自願且出於清醒意識，因此決定不起訴。檢察官表示自己未看過完整訪談紀錄，並稱將重啟調查；《紐約時報》取得的資訊則顯示，警方曾蒐集其他證據，但檢方沒有審閱，令外界質疑調查是否周全。案件也引發對紐約州法律的討論：若當事人因自行飲酒或用藥而失去同意能力，性侵案件可能較難起訴。

輿論壓力與兄弟會文化問題
